Phase 2 · Activation 3 — Original Concept

The Undercard

Before rival schools meet on the field, their quarterbacks meet in Fortnite.

6 Matchups Filmed October Released Rivalry Week $500K All-In
The Concept

The rivalry starts early

Every agency will pitch an athlete playing Fortnite in his room. That's a stream, not a campaign.

The Undercard gives the match something to be about. Two athletes from rival programs face off online — solo, or duos with the two best players from each side. Filmed through October, released into each rivalry's game week.

The tension is pre-loaded. We don't have to manufacture a reason to watch, because a hundred years of the rivalry already did it. Both fanbases are conscripted — every episode has two audiences invested in an outcome, and neither can ignore it.

Each athlete is captured locally with a real crew, so the cut is dual-POV: both faces, both screens, the moment it turns. Not a screen recording.

Episode Structure

One template. Six executions.

Every episode is built the same way. Nothing is reinvented between matchups — which is what makes it a system instead of six separate shoots.

01

The Callout

Each athlete calls out his rival to camera. Posted to both channels. This is the piece that travels.

02

The Match

Dual-feed. Both faces, both screens. Cut to the swings, not the gameplay.

03

The Result

Winner talks. Loser answers for it. Released into that rivalry's game week.

04

The Cutdowns

Vertical edits pushed across both athletes' platforms through game week.
